text:
Montreal outplayed Nashville for most of the night and lost by three goals, and the damage came in a stretch of 1 minute and 50 seconds late in the third. With the game tied at 2 and the Canadiens leading the shot-attempt count 65 to 45, Ryan O'Reilly tipped in a power-play goal at 16:44, and Adam Edstrom added two quick goals at 17:23 and 18:34. Edstrom's first came on a chance that carried an 84 percent probability of scoring, and his second was at 63 percent. Edstrom played only 10 minutes and 18 seconds yet finished with 1.52 individual expected goals.

The underlying numbers say Montreal controlled the game at even strength, 3.36 expected goals to 0.83, and the simulation gives the Canadiens a 78 percent chance of winning a replay of every shot. Nick Suzuki and Alex Newhook gave them a 2-0 lead in the second, but Nashville answered with Alexander Kerfoot's tip-in and a power-play snap from Matthew Wood in the final minute of the period. Montreal took 20 penalty minutes to Nashville's 6, and Nashville cashed in on two of five power plays, which is where most of its expected goals came from.

Juuse Saros was the other piece of the gap. He faced 33 shots and allowed two goals on 3.7 expected, saving 1.7 goals above what an average goalie would have. Jacob Fowler, at the other end, gave up three on 1.97 expected through 18 shots, and the three goals he allowed in the third turned a tie into a rout.
